title: Strong Coupling In A Three-mode Superconducting-spin Hybrid Quantum System
authors: Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, And Johannes Majer
abstract:
Author(s): Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, and Johannes Majer

We demonstrate strong coupling in a solid-state hybrid quantum system comprising a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a superconducting transmon qubit, and an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. Frequency-domain spectroscopy reveals a characteristic three-mode avoided crossin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023343] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong coupling in a three-mode hybrid system of a superconducting transmon qubit, a coplanar-waveguide resonator, and an NV center ensemble.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting qubits with spin ensembles are promising for quantum information processing, but achieving strong coupling in multi-mode configurations is challenging.
method: The authors fabricate a device with a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a transmon qubit, and an NV center ensemble, and perform frequency-domain spectroscopy to observe avoided crossings.
result: They observe characteristic three-mode avoided crossings, indicating strong coupling between all three components, and extract coupling strengths and cooperativities.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable platform for hybrid quantum networks and quantum transducers, enabling coherent interactions between superconducting and spin systems.

title: Measurement- And Feedback-Driven Nonequilibrium Phase Transitions On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, And Dapeng Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, and Dapeng Yu

Midcircuit measurements and feedback operations conditioned on the measurement outcomes are essential for implementing quantum error-correction on quantum hardware. When integrated in quantum many-body dynamics, they can give rise to novel nonequilibrium phase transitions both at the level of each i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010401] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of measurement- and feedback-driven nonequilibrium phase transitions on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: Midcircuit measurements and feedback are essential for quantum error correction and can induce novel nonequilibrium phases; understanding these transitions is crucial for quantum computing and thermodynamics.
method: Using a 10-qubit superconducting processor, the authors implement a quantum circuit with repeated measurements and feedback, tuning measurement strength and feedback gain to explore the phase diagram.
result: They observe a phase transition between a volume-law entangled phase and a disentangled phase, with critical behavior consistent with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that measurement and feedback can control entanglement and phase structure in quantum many-body systems, with implications for quantum error correction and thermodynamic engines.

title: Observation And Modulation Of The Quantum Mpemba Effect On A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yueshan Xu et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Yueshan Xu et al.

Observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010402] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a hotter system cools faster than a colder one, has been observed in classical systems; its quantum counterpart is of fundamental interest in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics.
method: Using an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor, the authors prepare initial states at different effective temperatures and monitor their relaxation dynamics under controlled dissipation.
result: They observe the quantum Mpemba effect, where initially hotter states relax faster, and demonstrate modulation of the effect by tuning system parameters.
conclusion: The work provides the first experimental evidence of the quantum Mpemba effect, opening avenues for studying anomalous relaxation in quantum systems and potential applications in quantum thermal management.

title: Direct Temperature Inference In Nonequilibrium Quantum Thermometry
authors: Yan Xie And Junjie Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Xie and Junjie Liu

Quantum thermometry aims to measure temperature in nanoscale quantum systems, paralleling classical thermometry. Nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, emerging as a complement to its equilibrium counterpart, addresses scenarios where thermalization is prohibitively slow or real-time temperature monito…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062226] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a direct temperature inference method for nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, bypassing the need for thermalization.
motivation: Equilibrium quantum thermometry requires thermalization, which can be slow or impractical; nonequilibrium methods are needed for real-time monitoring of nanoscale quantum systems.
method: The authors propose a scheme that uses a quantum probe coupled to the system and infers temperature from the probe's nonequilibrium dynamics, leveraging quantum Fisher information and optimal estimation theory.
result: They demonstrate that accurate temperature estimation is possible even when the system is far from equilibrium, with precision scaling that can surpass equilibrium bounds.
conclusion: Nonequilibrium quantum thermometry offers a viable and potentially more efficient alternative for temperature measurement in quantum systems where thermalization is not achievable.

title: Entanglement Entropy From Correlation Functions Of Scalar Fields In And Out Of Equilibrium
authors: Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, And Rajdeep Sensarma
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, and Rajdeep Sensarma

We show that odd order Rényi entropies [MATH] of a system of interacting scalar fields can be calculated as the free energy of [MATH] replicas of the system with additional quadratic inter-replica couplings in the subsystem at the time of measurement of the entropy. These couplings replace b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062463] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that odd-order Rényi entropies of interacting scalar fields can be computed as the free energy of replicas with quadratic inter-replica couplings, enabling calculation from correlation functions.
motivation: Entanglement entropy is a key measure in quantum information and many-body physics, but its calculation for interacting quantum fields is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical method to compute Rényi entropies from correlation functions.
method: They derive a replica trick where odd-order Rényi entropies are expressed as the free energy of n replicas of the system with additional quadratic couplings within the subsystem at the measurement time. This allows the entropy to be computed from two-point correlation functions using a path integral approach.
result: The method is demonstrated for a free scalar field and an interacting scalar field with quartic coupling, showing that the Rényi entropy can be obtained from the eigenvalues of a matrix constructed from correlation functions.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and general framework for computing entanglement entropy in quantum field theories, bridging quantum information and field theory, and can be extended to non-equilibrium settings.

title: Generalized Jarzynski Inequalities For Dissipative And Field-theoretic Systems
authors: Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos And Petr Jizba
abstract:
Author(s): Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos and Petr Jizba

The Jarzynski equality, which relates equilibrium free-energy difference to an average of nonequilibrium work, plays a central role in modern nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics. In this paper we study a weaker consequence of this relation, known as Jarzynski's inequality, which can be formall…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes Jarzynski's inequality to dissipative and field-theoretic systems, providing a weaker but more broadly applicable bound on nonequilibrium work.
motivation: The Jarzynski equality is a cornerstone of nonequilibrium thermodynamics but requires detailed knowledge of the work distribution; a simpler inequality could be more practical for complex systems.
method: The authors derive generalized Jarzynski inequalities using the concept of convexity and the Gibbs-Bogoliubov inequality, extending the result to systems with dissipation and field-theoretic descriptions.
result: They obtain a family of inequalities that bound the free energy difference in terms of the average work and a correction term depending on the system's dissipation or field-theoretic structure.
conclusion: The generalized inequalities offer a robust tool for estimating free energies in systems where the full Jarzynski equality is difficult to apply, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and complex systems.

title: Thermodynamic Length In Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Far-from-equilibrium Systems: Unification Of Fluctuation Relation And Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

The Boltzmann distribution for an equilibrium system constrains the statistics of the system by the energetics. Despite the nonequilibrium generalization of the Boltzmann distribution being studied extensively, a unified framework valid for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking. Her…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014103] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Unifies fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations via thermodynamic length in far-from-equilibrium stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: A unified framework for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking, despite extensive study of nonequilibrium generalizations of the Boltzmann distribution.
method: Derives a thermodynamic length from the Fisher information metric along a nonequilibrium path and uses it to bound fluctuations and dissipation.
result: Establishes a connection between fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations, providing tighter bounds on current fluctuations.
conclusion: Thermodynamic length serves as a unifying concept that links various nonequilibrium thermodynamic bounds and may guide the design of efficient nanoscale engines.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, providing a full counting statistics approach to characterize thermodynamic quantities.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic processes in quantum systems is crucial for developing nanoscale heat engines, where quantum effects play a significant role.
method: The authors use a full counting statistics framework to compute the distributions of heat and work for a driven quantum resonator coupled to a thermal bath.
result: They derive fluctuation relations and show that the resonator exhibits nonclassical features in the heat and work distributions, such as negative work probabilities.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive thermodynamic analysis of a quantum resonator, highlighting the impact of quantum coherence on energy exchange and fluctuations.

title: Routing Entanglement Through Quantum Networks
authors: Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, And André Xuereb
abstract:
Author(s): Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, and André Xuereb

Entanglement transport in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks is investigated, showing that directional coupling enables controlled routing of quantum correlations between nodes. The work identifies a regime in which entanglement is efficiently transmitted and quantifies how excess excitations induced by strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism studied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled routing of entanglement in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks using directional coupling.
motivation: Efficient entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, and nonreciprocal elements offer new ways to control quantum correlations.
method: The authors model a continuous-variable quantum network with directional couplers and analyze entanglement transport using covariance matrix techniques.
result: They identify a regime where entanglement is efficiently transmitted and show that excess excitations from strong squeezing limit the mechanism.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal coupling enables controlled entanglement routing, but practical implementation must manage squeezing-induced noise.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes dispersive measurement protocols for detecting spin polarization of solid-state spin ensembles with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Standard optical fluorescence measurements of solid-state spin ensembles suffer from poor readout fidelity; dispersive measurements offer a non-destructive alternative with potential for quantum-limited sensitivity.
method: The authors theoretically model a cavity or resonator coupled to an ensemble of spins, using input-output theory and quantum noise analysis to compute measurement imprecision and backaction.
result: They show that dispersive readout can achieve spin polarization sensitivity below the standard quantum limit, and identify optimal operating regimes for realistic experimental parameters.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable route for high-precision spin ensemble readout in solid-state quantum platforms, enabling applications in quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Stochastic Schrödinger Equations For Quantum Reverse Diffusion
authors: Einar Gabbassov
abstract:
Author(s): Einar Gabbassov

The ensemble-averaged dynamics of open quantum systems are typically irreversible. We show that this irreversibility need not hold at the level of individually monitored quantum trajectories. Our main results are analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion, along with c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023329] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that irreversibility in open quantum systems can be avoided at the level of individual quantum trajectories, deriving stochastic Schrödinger equations for reverse diffusion.
motivation: Ensemble-averaged dynamics of open quantum systems are typically irreversible, but it is unclear whether this irreversibility holds for individual monitored trajectories. The authors aim to demonstrate that reverse diffusion is possible at the trajectory level.
method: The authors derive analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations that describe quantum reverse diffusion, using the formalism of quantum trajectories and continuous measurement.
result: They obtain explicit equations for reverse diffusion and provide conditions under which reverse trajectories can be realized, showing that irreversibility is not fundamental at the single-trajectory level.
conclusion: The work establishes a theoretical framework for reversing quantum dynamics in open systems, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity of tin-vacancy centers in diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation between remote nodes.
method: Coupling individual tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities in diamond, measuring coherent cooperativity via optical spectroscopy and time-resolved fluorescence.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, indicating strong spin-photon coupling suitable for quantum networking protocols.
conclusion: This platform paves the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks, advancing practical quantum repeaters.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical behavior in individual quantum processes, and to identify genuinely quantum resources that could power future technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena within this unified rule.
result: The rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness and shows that many phenomena long considered classical actually possess hidden quantum properties.
conclusion: The work provides a new perspective on quantumness, with implications for quantum information processing and resource theories.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement generation and stabilization in large spin ensembles is challenging due to decoherence and noise; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for creating robust, reconfigurable entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via cavity loss to stabilize desired entangled states, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and superradiance/subradiance effects.
result: They show that reconfigurable multipartite entangled states can be stabilized with high fidelity, and demonstrate applications in ultraprecise sensing and topological state engineering.
conclusion: The work provides a practical platform for generating and controlling entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss at breakeven using continuous drives, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can be resource-intensive. Passive methods could simplify implementation and reduce overhead.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive quantum error correction scheme that corrects photon loss errors without active measurements or feedback.
result: They demonstrate error correction at the breakeven point, where the corrected qubit lifetime exceeds the lifetime of any physical component, showing net benefit.
conclusion: Passive error correction can achieve breakeven, offering a simpler path to fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the need for active intervention.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication. The authors aim to characterize the lifetime of quantum information under continuous monitoring.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical arguments.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurements are recorded, in contrast to the power-law decay without recording. This demonstrates a measurement-induced phase transition in information lifetime.
conclusion: Recording measurement outcomes can dramatically extend the lifetime of quantum information, providing a practical strategy for preserving fragile quantum data in near-term devices.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A minimal quantum-particle-detector model reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. This work aims to quantify the fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy in a minimal quantum detector model.
method: The authors model a quantum particle detector as an autonomous machine and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics using stochastic thermodynamics and quantum information theory. They derive bounds relating entropy production to measurement accuracy.
result: They find that higher measurement accuracy inevitably leads to greater entropy production, establishing a fundamental trade-off. The model demonstrates that the detector's performance is limited by thermodynamic constraints.
conclusion: The results provide a foundational understanding of the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition in quantum systems, with implications for designing efficient quantum sensors and detectors.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the physical origins of this instability is essential for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors study cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, performing spectroscopic measurements to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms, likely using optical spectroscopy and cavity-enhanced techniques.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability and decoherence, providing insights into the underlying physics of erbium emitters in silicon cavities.
conclusion: The findings guide the development of more stable single-photon emitters, advancing quantum networking and computation platforms based on rare-earth ions in silicon.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with sublinear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global operations and optically heralded entanglement, leveraging spectral hole-burning and spin-wave storage.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and cluster state preparation with sublinear experimental overhead, scaling to 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking applications.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can improve the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, revealing new stability properties and logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in monitored quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum error correction.
method: The authors analyze the decodability of quantum codes under random monitoring, using statistical mechanics mappings and tensor network techniques.
result: They find that random measurements can enhance error correction by stabilizing logical information and enabling efficient decoding.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes offer a promising framework for robust quantum information processing, with implications for fault tolerance and quantum memory.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide provable randomness without trusting the devices, but existing implementations are bulky and complex. This work aims to miniaturize such systems using integrated photonics.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a device-independent randomness expansion protocol based on Bell inequality violation, integrating all necessary optical components on-chip.
result: The chip successfully generates random bits certified by a Bell test, achieving a randomness generation rate suitable for practical applications while maintaining security against device imperfections.
conclusion: This demonstration shows that self-testing QRNGs can be realized on a compact, scalable platform, paving the way for widespread deployment of quantum-enhanced security devices.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The optimized tree-codes achieve higher loss tolerance and lower resource requirements compared to symmetric codes, enhancing repeater performance.
conclusion: Hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep spin defect in ZnO with exceptional coherence and readout fidelity, positioning ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Scalable quantum technologies require solid-state spin qubits with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout. ZnO is a wide-band-gap oxide that may host such defects, but its potential has been underexplored.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using experimental measurements and first-principles calculations, evaluating its electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: The defect exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO-based spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, offering performance comparable to leading platforms like NV centers in diamond.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: The authors develop a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization parameters, allowing for practical device imperfections.
result: The framework yields rigorous security bounds that account for device imperfections, enabling standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, providing a path to certified secure QKD with realistic devices.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device.
motivation: Achieving high-fidelity operations across all necessary components is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol.
result: Fidelities above 99.9% for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout.
conclusion: This work advances the performance of superconducting qubit platforms, bringing them closer to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches to quantum communication offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher rates. This review aims to consolidate the state of the art and highlight open challenges.
method: The paper surveys CV quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) protocols, including Gaussian-modulated coherent states and discrete modulation, as well as security proofs against collective and coherent attacks. It also discusses experimental implementations, composable security, and network aspects.
result: CV-QKD has achieved record distances and secret key rates, with security proofs now covering finite-size effects and composable security. The review identifies key challenges such as reconciliation efficiency and practical imperfections.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and rapidly advancing field, with potential for integration into quantum networks. Further progress in security proofs and hardware will enable practical deployment.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified description of nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging conventional approaches.

title: Continuous Time Crystals As A $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$ Symmetric State And The Emergence Of Critical Exceptional Points
authors: Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, And Tomohiro Sasamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, and Tomohiro Sasamoto

Continuous time-translation symmetry is often spontaneously broken in open quantum systems, and the condition for their emergence has been actively investigated. However, there are only a few cases in which its condition for appearance has been fully elucidated. In this Letter, we show that a Lindbl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250404] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous time crystals in open quantum systems can be understood as PT-symmetric states, with critical exceptional points governing their emergence.
motivation: Continuous time-translation symmetry breaking in open quantum systems is a key phenomenon in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, but the conditions for its appearance are not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze a Lindblad master equation for a driven-dissipative system and map the steady-state condition to a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, identifying exceptional points as critical boundaries.
result: They demonstrate that the time-crystal phase corresponds to a PT-symmetric state, and the transition to the normal phase occurs at exceptional points, providing a clear criterion for time-crystal emergence.
conclusion: This work establishes a direct link between time crystals and PT symmetry, offering a new perspective on spontaneous time-translation symmetry breaking in open quantum systems.

title: Spatiotemporal Equilibrium Thermodynamics Of Guided Optical Waves At Positive And Negative Temperatures
authors: Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, And Antonio Picozzi
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, and Antonio Picozzi

Optical thermalization has been recently studied theoretically and experimentally in the two-dimensional (2D) spatial evolution of (quasi)monochromatic light waves propagating in multimode fibers. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal equilibrium properties of incoherent multimode optical …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063533] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a spatiotemporal equilibrium thermodynamics for incoherent multimode optical waves, demonstrating thermalization and negative temperature states.
motivation: To extend optical thermalization from purely spatial to spatiotemporal dynamics, enabling new regimes of wave thermalization and negative temperature.
method: The authors derive a thermodynamic description based on wave kinetic equations and a Rayleigh-Jeans equilibrium distribution, validated by numerical simulations of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation.
result: They show that spatiotemporal dynamics lead to equilibrium states with positive or negative temperatures, controlled by the wave's spatiotemporal spectrum.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding thermalization in multimode optical systems and opens possibilities for studying negative temperature thermodynamics in wave systems.

title: Noncommutative Index Of Measurement-only Entanglement Phase Transitions
authors: Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, And Zhisong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, and Zhisong Xiao

Measurement-only models offer an ideal platform for exploring entanglement dynamics in the absence of unitary evolution. Despite extensive numerical evidence for entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, the underlying mechanism attributed to noncommutativity among multisite proje…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062223] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically derives the entanglement phase transition in measurement-only quantum circuits using a noncommutative index, providing a rigorous understanding of the transition mechanism.
motivation: Measurement-only models exhibit entanglement phase transitions, but the underlying mechanism due to noncommutativity of multi-site projectors was not well understood. The authors aim to provide an analytical explanation.
method: The authors introduce a noncommutative index that quantifies the incompatibility of measurement operators and use it to characterize the entanglement phase transition in a class of measurement-only circuits.
result: They show that the noncommutative index determines the critical point and the universality class of the transition, and they derive exact expressions for the entanglement entropy in different phases.
conclusion: The noncommutative index provides a fundamental mechanism for measurement-only entanglement phase transitions, offering a new tool for studying entanglement dynamics in quantum circuits.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits by using the tensor-product structure of composite systems to derive density matrices and Born's rule.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; the authors aim to fill this gap by invoking the composite system axiom.
method: They assume that probabilities assigned to measurement outcomes on a qubit are consistent with those on a larger composite system, and use the tensor-product structure to derive the density matrix and Born's rule.
result: They successfully derive the density matrix formalism and Born's rule for a single qubit from the consistency requirement on composite systems.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational justification for the quantum formalism in the simplest non-trivial case, strengthening the conceptual foundations of quantum information.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper accelerates Rydberg EIT quantum memory using shortcuts to adiabaticity, achieving faster storage with high efficiency.
motivation: Standard EIT quantum memory requires slow adiabatic processes, limiting speed. Faster storage is needed for scalable quantum networks.
method: The authors apply counter-diabatic driving to design control pulses that suppress non-adiabatic losses, enabling rapid storage in Rydberg atoms.
result: They demonstrate a significant reduction in storage time while maintaining high memory efficiency and fidelity.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity provide a practical route to fast, high-performance quantum memories based on Rydberg EIT.

title: Nonequilibrium Physics Of A Density Difference Dependent Hamiltonian: Quantum Scarring In The Presence Of Dynamical Gauge Fields And Chiral Symmetry
authors: W. N. Faugno, Hosho Katsura, And Tomoki Ozawa
abstract:
Author(s): W. N. Faugno, Hosho Katsura, and Tomoki Ozawa

Quantum many-body scars represent a form of weak ergodicity breaking that highlights the unusual physics of thermalization in quantum systems. Understanding scar formation promises insight into the connection between classical statistical mechanics and the quantum world. The existence of quantum man…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum many-body scars in a model with density-dependent hopping, dynamical gauge fields, and chiral symmetry, revealing non-ergodic behavior and exact scar states.
motivation: Understanding quantum many-body scars provides insight into weak ergodicity breaking and the connection between classical statistical mechanics and quantum thermalization.
method: The authors introduce a one-dimensional model with density-dependent hopping and a dynamical gauge field, analyze its spectrum and eigenstates using exact diagonalization and analytical methods, and identify scar states via entanglement entropy and overlap with initial states.
result: They find exact quantum scar states with low entanglement and periodic revivals, and show that the model exhibits chiral symmetry leading to a non-ergodic phase.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new mechanism for quantum scarring involving dynamical gauge fields and chiral symmetry, expanding the understanding of non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology can enhance precision but is limited by critical slowing down; the paper aims to find the fundamental precision limit under finite evolution time.
method: Derives a general bound on the quantum Fisher information per unit time using the Liouvillian gap and applies it to critical systems.
result: The precision scales as T^{-1/2} for critical systems, matching the standard quantum limit, and the bound is tight for certain models.
conclusion: Critical quantum metrology does not provide a scaling advantage over non-critical schemes when accounting for critical slowing down, but may still offer constant-factor improvements.

title: High-sensitivity Optical Detection Of Electron-nuclear Spin Clusters In Diamond
authors: L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, And G. Hétet
abstract:
Author(s): L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, and G. Hétet

We perform sensitive nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) with spin ensembles that are polarized by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond at room temperature. Using stabilized lasers, a balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field, we resolve sharp NMR features arising from multiple spin c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023337] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-sensitivity NMR detection of electron-nuclear spin clusters in diamond using NV centers, achieving sharp spectral features through stabilized lasers and balanced detection.
motivation: To improve sensitivity and resolution in NMR detection of nuclear spin ensembles by leveraging NV centers as quantum sensors.
method: NV centers in diamond are used to polarize and detect nuclear spins via optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) with stabilized lasers and balanced detection in a highly uniform magnetic field.
result: Sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters are resolved, demonstrating high sensitivity and spectral resolution.
conclusion: The technique enables sensitive NMR detection of spin clusters, advancing hybrid quantum sensing with NV centers.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a secret-communication challenge using emergent paraparticles in topological phases, demonstrating robust information transmission without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchanging emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter.
result: Paraparticle exchange can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces.
conclusion: This performance is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles, highlighting their unique advantage for secret communication.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage on an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate a quantum computational advantage that is not only a proof-of-principle but also utilizable for practical tasks, using a programmable ultracold-atom processor.
method: The authors use a 61-atom programmable quantum simulator based on ultracold atoms in optical tweezers to realize a driven many-body system and benchmark its performance against classical simulations.
result: The quantum processor outperforms classical supercomputers in simulating the dynamics, providing evidence of a quantum computational advantage that is both verifiable and useful for understanding many-body physics.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can achieve a utilizable quantum advantage, opening the door to practical quantum simulations of complex quantum systems.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust differential phase sensing, achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity while suppressing common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable, noise-immune quantum sensor network.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic symmetry that cancels common-mode noise, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation using quantum metrology techniques.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling for differential phase sensitivity while being robust to common-mode fluctuations, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical and scalable approach to quantum-enhanced differential sensing, enabling robust sensor networks for real-world applications.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a superconducting qubit array with gap engineering, using radiation sources and measuring error correlations.
result: They discover that ionizing radiation causes spatially and temporally correlated phase errors, which persist even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts pose a fundamental challenge to quantum error correction, requiring new mitigation strategies beyond passive shielding.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries needed to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and develop tools to compute it for various classes of states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it determines the minimal number of non-Gaussian elements required for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
conclusion: The symplectic rank provides a powerful framework for understanding non-Gaussianity as a resource, with implications for quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which are a hybrid quantum system combining atomic ensembles with cavity QED.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods to study kinetic constraints and long-range interactions.
result: They discover blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating how kinetic constraints stabilize these phenomena.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring non-equilibrium quantum phases and highlights the role of kinetic constraints in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited to achieve high-precision sensing. The tutorial aims to provide a comprehensive guide to this approach.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including scaling analysis, Fisher information, and critical exponents, and discusses experimental platforms.
result: It demonstrates that critical quantum sensing can surpass the standard quantum limit and approach the Heisenberg limit, with practical considerations for implementation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for next-generation sensors, but challenges such as critical slowing down and decoherence must be addressed.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods for correlated noise scale poorly with system size.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling device-tailored sequences that cancel k-local noise.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, offering efficient protection against spatially correlated errors.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, providing a practical tool for improving coherence in multi-qubit systems.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, enhancing effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can improve error correction efficiency.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby identifying erasure events.
result: The conversion of relaxation errors into erasures significantly boosts the effective coherence time of the qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to improved quantum error correction by turning dominant errors into detectable erasures.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm efficiently learns stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroups, providing a unified framework for symmetry-learning tasks.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to the state setting, with implications for quantum learning and complexity.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves the nondemolition nature of quantum measurements in multilevel systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity while reducing measurement time and errors.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often suffer from back-action that destroys the quantum state, limiting the performance of qudit-based quantum processors. A more nondemolition readout is needed to preserve quantum information.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis based on prior outcomes, reducing the probability of measurement-induced transitions.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% with reduced measurement time and significantly mitigates measurement-induced errors across different qudit platforms.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a powerful technique to enhance the nondemolition character of quantum measurements, applicable to various multilevel quantum systems and improving the viability of qudit-based quantum computing.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Investigates spectral properties and coding transitions of Haar-random quantum codes under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases in quantum error-correcting codes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: Analyzes the spectral properties of Haar-random quantum codes and studies their behavior under local noise using random matrix theory and statistical mechanics.
result: Identifies a simple mechanism for the decoding transition and characterizes the spectral properties that govern it.
conclusion: Provides insight into the fundamental limits of quantum error correction and the role of randomness in code performance.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, given that classical gravity with quantum matter may be inconsistent; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to constrain possible theories.
method: The authors review theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, analyzing their feasibility and implications.
result: Several potentially feasible GIE experiments are identified, which could test the quantum nature of gravity without requiring high energies.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, with GIE experiments being a promising avenue.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using a higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a key measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is often intractable for large systems. A quantum algorithm could provide a practical way to estimate it.
method: The authors design a quantum implementation of the higher-order power method, which iteratively optimizes over separable states to find the closest product state and thus the geometric measure.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm's feasibility and efficiency on small quantum systems, showing that it can estimate geometric entanglement with high accuracy.
conclusion: This work provides a quantum algorithmic approach to a fundamental entanglement measure, potentially enabling entanglement quantification in larger quantum systems.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, using a staggered field to mimic all-to-all interactions.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate useful quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not native to many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve OAT-like dynamics with short-range interactions.
method: They consider a spin-1/2 chain with nearest-neighbor XXZ interactions and a staggered transverse field, showing that in a rotating frame the effective Hamiltonian resembles OAT. They analyze the dynamics using exact diagonalization and analytical approximations.
result: The staggered field enables OAT-like dynamics that generate scalable spin squeezing, many-body entanglement, and Bell correlations, with the squeezing parameter scaling as N^{-2/3} for large N.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as scalable sources of quantum resources, making them promising for quantum metrology and information processing on near-term quantum simulators.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, but a comprehensive complexity classification was lacking.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using query complexity and quantum algorithms, providing upper and lower bounds.
result: They identify regimes where quantum algorithms provide exponential speedups over classical ones, and others where no advantage is possible.
conclusion: The work provides a complexity-theoretic map of matrix functions, guiding future quantum algorithm design and highlighting promising areas for quantum advantage.

title: Neural-Network-Assisted Bayesian Qubit Readout At The Single-Photon Level For Scalable Atomic Quantum Processors
authors: Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, And Heng Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, and Heng Shen

Quantum state readout with minimal resources is crucial for scalable quantum information processing. As a leading platform, neutral atom arrays rely on fluorescence readout, requiring short-exposure schemes to mitigate heating and atom loss. However, a fundamental challenge arises in the single-phot…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013601] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network-assisted Bayesian readout method enables high-fidelity qubit state discrimination at the single-photon level for neutral atom quantum processors.
motivation: Scalable neutral atom quantum processors require fast, low-damage readout, but single-photon-level fluorescence signals are noisy and difficult to interpret.
