Here, the authors develop a microscopic theory of dispersing anyons in fractional quantum anomalous Hall systems and a momentum-space Monte Carlo framework to evaluate quasihole energies. By constructing momentum-resolved Laughlin quasihole states in Aharonov-Casher bands, they compute anyon bandwidths relevant to twisted MoTe
[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235155] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a microscopic theory of dispersing anyons in fractional quantum anomalous Hall systems, focusing on twisted MoTe2.
motivation: Understanding anyon dispersion is crucial for realizing itinerant anyon phases, but previous models assumed flat bands; this work accounts for nonuniform quantum geometry.
method: The authors construct momentum-resolved Laughlin quasihole states in Aharonov-Casher bands and use a momentum-space Monte Carlo framework to compute quasihole energies and bandwidths.
result: They show that nonuniform quantum geometry combined with the quasihole Berry phase leads to finite anyon dispersion, and compute relevant bandwidths for twisted MoTe2.
conclusion: The work provides a controlled route to study itinerant anyon phases and highlights the role of quantum geometry in anyon dynamics.

title: Magnetoexcitons And Massive Dirac Fermions In Monolayers Of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides In A High Magnetic Field

tldr: A theoretical study of magnetoexciton emission spectra in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides under high magnetic fields, focusing on interactions with quantum Hall states of massive Dirac fermions.
motivation: To understand the optical properties of transition metal dichalcogenides in strong magnetic fields, which is relevant for condensed matter physics but not directly for quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Uses an ab initio-parametrized massive Dirac fermion model including valley and spin degrees of freedom to compute the emission spectrum of magnetoexcitons interacting with quantum Hall states.
result: Predicts specific features in the emission spectrum due to magnetoexciton–quantum Hall state interactions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into many-body effects in two-dimensional semiconductors under high magnetic fields, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Anomalous Quasiparticle Lifetime In Geometric Quantum Critical Metals
authors: Hao Song, Han Ma, Catherine Kallin, And Sung-Sik Lee
abstract:

Metals can undergo geometric quantum phase transitions where the local curvature of the Fermi surface changes sign without a change in symmetry or topology. At the inflection points on the Fermi surface, the local curvature vanishes, leading to an anomalous dynamics of quasiparticles. In this paper,…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245148] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quasiparticle lifetime in metals at geometric quantum critical points where Fermi surface curvature vanishes.
motivation: Understanding how quasiparticles behave when the Fermi surface curvature changes sign, which is a novel type of quantum phase transition.
method: The authors use field-theoretic methods to compute the quasiparticle self-energy and lifetime near inflection points on the Fermi surface.
result: They find that the quasiparticle lifetime exhibits anomalous scaling due to the vanishing curvature, leading to non-Fermi liquid behavior.
conclusion: Geometric quantum critical points give rise to new universal dynamics distinct from conventional quantum critical points.

title: Kondo Effect In Ferromagnetic Quantum Critical ${\mathrm{CeRh}}_{6}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{4}$

tldr: This paper studies the Kondo effect and quantum criticality in a heavy-fermion ferromagnet using spectroscopic techniques.
motivation: To understand the nature of cerium's 4f electron and its role in pressure-induced quantum criticality in CeRh6Ge4.
method: Combined core-level photoemission and polarized x-ray absorption spectroscopy with single-impurity Anderson model simulations.
result: Kondo hybridization admixes higher-lying crystal field states into a multiorbital ground state with 4f occupancy ~0.9, explaining the dynamical spin response.
conclusion: Kondo hybridization and multiorbital ground state are essential for modeling quantum criticality in this system.

motivation: Recent experiments observed the Yamaji effect in underdoped cuprates, indicating small hole pockets; this paper aims to model and explain these observations.
method: The authors use theoretical models of underdoped cuprates to analyze angle-dependent magnetoresistance and the Yamaji effect.
result: The paper provides evidence for small hole pockets in the pseudogap regime consistent with experimental observations.
conclusion: The findings support the existence of hole pockets and help understand the pseudogap phase in cuprates.

authors: Meita Asami, Kentaroh Watanabe, And Masakazu Sugiyama

In this study, we investigate the interpretation of the Stokes shift (SS) by employing the optoelectronic reciprocity relation (ORR), which provides a fundamental link between optical absorption and emission processes. We first revisit the van Roosbroeck-Shockley relation and the generalized Planck'…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245310] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the Stokes shift in semiconductors using the optoelectronic reciprocity relation, linking absorption and emission.
motivation: To understand the origin of the Stokes shift, a key phenomenon in luminescent materials, by bridging absorption and emission through a fundamental relation.
method: The authors revisit the van Roosbroeck-Shockley relation and generalized Planck's law, applying the optoelectronic reciprocity relation to analyze the Stokes shift.
result: They provide a reinterpretation of the Stokes shift based on the reciprocity relation, clarifying its connection to non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
conclusion: The optoelectronic reciprocity relation offers a unified framework for understanding the Stokes shift, with implications for semiconductor device physics.

motivation: Improving hydrogen storage capacity is important for energy applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use computational modeling and inelastic neutron scattering to analyze hydrogen behavior in fullerenelike nanoporous carbon.
result: They find a highly dense phase of hydrogen at temperatures above the melting point, but the work is purely materials science.
conclusion: The findings are relevant to hydrogen storage but not to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

This work extends the universal finite-size scaling framework for continuum percolation from two-dimensional (2D) to quasi-three-dimensional (Q3D) stick systems, in which sequentially deposited wires of finite diameter stack vertically on a flat substrate. Using Monte Carlo simulation, the percolati…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014102] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-size scaling in quasi-three-dimensional stick percolation using Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding percolation in quasi-3D systems is important for applications like conductive nanowire networks, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Monte Carlo simulations of sequentially deposited finite-diameter wires on a flat substrate, extending a 2D scaling framework to quasi-3D.
result: The universal finite-size scaling framework is extended to quasi-3D stick systems, and percolation thresholds are characterized.
conclusion: The work provides a scaling theory for quasi-3D continuum percolation, but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Frustration-induced Collective Dynamical States In Pulse-coupled Adaptive Winfree Networks

We investigate collective dynamics in a pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree network under the influence of a frustration (phase-lag) parameter. [Phys. Rev. E 114, 014201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree networks with frustration, focusing on frequency clustering and synchronization.
motivation: To understand how frustration (phase-lag) and Hebbian adaptation affect collective states in oscillator networks.
method: Numerical simulations of a pulse-coupled Winfree network with adaptive coupling strengths following a Hebbian rule, varying the frustration parameter.
result: Observation of frequency-clustered states, chimera states, and other collective dynamical regimes depending on frustration and adaptation.
conclusion: Frustration induces rich collective dynamics in adaptive oscillator networks, relevant to neural and biological systems.

title: Quantized Dynamical Pumping Via Dissipation In A Mechanical Thouless Pump
authors: Marius Jürgensen And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Marius Jürgensen and Mikael C. Rechtsman

Thouless pumps are time-periodic one-dimensional systems that capture the physics of the two-dimensional quantum Hall effect via the quantized pumping of particles under adiabatic modulation. Recent work in photonics has shown that nonlinearity can act to quantize the displacement of light in the fo…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064154] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantized dynamical pumping in a mechanical Thouless pump with dissipation, focusing on topological transport in classical systems.
motivation: To understand how dissipation affects the quantized pumping of particles in a Thouless pump, extending topological concepts to classical dissipative systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a mechanical Thouless pump model incorporating dissipation, using Floquet theory and numerical simulations to study particle transport.
result: They find that dissipation can lead to quantized pumping even in the presence of loss, with the quantization being robust under certain conditions.
conclusion: Dissipation does not necessarily destroy quantized pumping but can instead enable it, offering new insights into topological transport in open systems.

title: Approach To Network Failure Due To Intrinsic Fluctuations
authors: Shaunak Roy, Vimal Kishore, And M. S. Santhanam

tldr: This paper studies network failure due to intrinsic fluctuations in node flux, modeled as random walkers and extreme events.
motivation: Understanding how intrinsic fluctuations in network traffic can lead to node failures is important for network reliability.
method: The authors model flux as random walkers and treat large fluctuations as extreme events to identify three distinct nodal failure regimes.
result: Three distinct nodal failure regimes are identified based on the statistics of fluctuations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting network failures arising solely from intrinsic fluctuations.

title: Van Hove Singularities In The Density Of States Of A Chaotic Dynamical System
authors: Bryn Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Bryn Davies

We show that the statistics of chaotic systems can be predicted by constructing an associated sequence of periodic differential operators and computing their densities of states. For such operators, the density of states is well understood and can be computed straightforwardly, often yielding explic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064211] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts chaotic system statistics using periodic differential operators and their density of states, revealing Van Hove singularities.
motivation: To understand and predict statistical properties of chaotic dynamical systems through an analogy with periodic differential operators.
method: Constructs an associated sequence of periodic differential operators and computes their densities of states, then relates these to the chaotic system's statistics.
result: The density of states for such operators can be computed straightforwardly, often yielding explicit formulas that reveal Van Hove singularities.
conclusion: The statistics of chaotic systems can be predicted using the well-understood density of states of periodic differential operators.

title: Controlling Synchronization Dynamics Via Physics-informed Neural Networks
authors: Kaiming Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiming Luo

Synchronization control in networked dynamical systems requires regulating not only whether coherence is achieved but also when and to what extent it emerges. We propose a physics-informed neural network framework for continuous-time synchronization regulation, in which system trajectories and contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064212] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses physics-informed neural networks to control synchronization dynamics in networked systems.
motivation: Synchronization control in networked dynamical systems requires regulating not only whether coherence is achieved but also when and to what extent it emerges.
method: A physics-informed neural network framework is proposed for continuous-time synchronization regulation, incorporating system trajectories and control constraints.
result: The framework enables precise control over synchronization timing and degree in networked systems.
conclusion: Physics-informed neural networks offer a flexible approach for synchronization control in complex networks.

title: Electronic Access To Glass Transition In Supercooled Ionic Liquids Using Ambipolar Transistor

Relaxation dynamics of supercooled liquids approaching glassy arrest remain a central challenge in integrated electronic architectures, where conventional rheometry becomes incompatible. Here, we demonstrate that an ambipolar [MATH] field-effect transistor functions as an electrical p…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065425] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses an ambipolar transistor to probe the glass transition in supercooled ionic liquids, demonstrating an electronic method to study relaxation dynamics.
motivation: Conventional rheometry is incompatible with integrated electronic architectures, so an electronic approach is needed to study glassy dynamics in supercooled ionic liquids.
method: An ambipolar field-effect transistor is fabricated with supercooled ionic liquids as the channel material, and its electrical characteristics are measured as a function of temperature to detect the glass transition.
result: The transistor's electrical response shows a clear signature of the glass transition, providing an electronic access to relaxation dynamics.
conclusion: Electronic devices can serve as sensitive probes for glass transition phenomena, offering a new tool for studying supercooled liquids in integrated platforms.

motivation: Understanding relaxation dynamics in low-dimensional materials is important for thermal management and nanomechanical resonator design.
method: The authors investigate intrinsic relaxation of armchair CNTs under single-mode excitation using theoretical modeling.
result: They identify mode coupling and resonance-induced relaxation mechanisms.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into thermal transport and coherence control in carbon nanotubes.

Hypergraphs provide a natural representation of complex systems with higher-order interactions and are commonly interdependent with each other. In this work, based on a bipartite network representation of hypergraphs, we propose a framework of networks of hypergraphs (NOH) to describe the structures…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064312] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework for networks of hypergraphs to study robustness against node failures.
motivation: Real-world systems often involve interdependent hypergraphs, but existing models do not capture such structures.
method: The authors model hypergraphs as bipartite networks and define a network of hypergraphs (NOH) to represent interdependencies, then analyze robustness via percolation theory.
result: They find that NOH can exhibit both enhanced and reduced robustness compared to isolated hypergraphs, depending on the coupling strength and degree distributions.
conclusion: The framework provides insights into the robustness of complex systems with higher-order interactions and interdependencies.

motivation: Organic mixed conductors have applications in bioelectronics and thermoelectrics, but their complex multi-scale dynamics are not well understood.
method: The author develops a lattice gas model and analyzes phase transitions using statistical mechanics techniques.
result: The model predicts phase transitions driven by the coupling between electronic and ionic degrees of freedom.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding the statistical mechanics of organic mixed conductors, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Steady-state Equilibrium And Nonequilibrium Noisy Network Dynamics
authors: Pik-Yin Lai

The fluctuating dynamics of a network about its stable, noise-free steady state are theoretically investigated. motivation: To understand how network connectivity and noise properties lead to nonequilibrium steady states.
method: Theoretical analysis using Langevin equations and covariance matrices to characterize fluctuations around a stable steady state.
result: Identifies conditions for equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics based on network symmetry and noise correlations.
conclusion: The framework provides a general classification of steady-state network dynamics but does not address quantum or information-theoretic aspects.

authors: Thierry Njougouo, Timoteo Carletti, And Elio Tuci

motivation: Understanding how group interactions influence opinion dynamics is fundamental to collective behavior, and higher-order structures beyond pairwise interactions are increasingly recognized as important.
method: The authors propose a model of opinion dynamics on d-uniform hypergraphs, where individuals interact through group-based structures, and analyze the model using analytical and numerical methods.
result: The model reveals how higher-order interactions affect consensus and polarization, showing that the structure of hypergraphs can significantly alter the dynamics compared to simple graphs.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions play a crucial role in collective decision-making, and hypergraph models provide a more accurate framework for studying such phenomena.

title: Nonreciprocal Blume-Capel Model With Antisymmetric Single-ion Anisotropies

motivation: To understand the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species spin model.
method: Combines systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions.
result: Maps the dynamical phase diagram of the model, revealing novel phases driven by nonreciprocity.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal interactions can lead to rich nonequilibrium behavior in classical spin systems.

tldr: This paper studies rigidity percolation dynamics on triangular lattices using an event-based ensemble Monte Carlo method.
motivation: Rigidity percolation is important for understanding mechanical stability in disordered materials, but most studies focus on static properties; the dynamics of the transition remain unexplored.
method: The authors employ an event-based ensemble approach to simulate the dynamic evolution of rigidity percolation on triangular lattices.
result: They characterize the dynamic critical behavior and identify the universality class of the rigidity percolation transition.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dynamic aspects of rigidity percolation, which may inform the design of disordered materials with tailored mechanical properties.

tldr: This paper develops effective collective coordinate models for kink dynamics in a driven-damped φ^4 model, extending a previous sine-Gordon approach.
motivation: To provide a reduced description of kink motion in the φ^4 model under driving and damping, which is important for understanding nonlinear wave dynamics in classical field theories.
method: Three reduced models based on kink position, width, and internal mode amplitude are derived using collective coordinate techniques and compared with full partial differential equation simulations.

conclusion: The collective coordinate approach offers a computationally efficient way to model kink dynamics, but its accuracy depends on the specific regime and choice of coordinates.

title: Relations Among Different Inequality Measures In Complex Systems: From Kinetic Exchange To Earthquake Models
