Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, focusing on magnetic order transitions.
motivation: To understand and control the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2, which is a topological phase of matter.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to probe the electronic structure and magnetic order.
result: Observation of a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control over ferromagnetic to antiferromagnetic transitions.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a platform for studying quantum anomalous Hall states with tunable magnetic order.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to detect anisotropy and its response to heat treatment.
result: They find hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, informing coating design and postprocessing strategies.
conclusion: The findings guide improved coating deposition and annealing to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, and Liuyan Zhao

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between different ferroic orders (polar, chiral, ferro-rotational) in a single material and the formation of complex domain walls.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were applied to Ni₂MnSbO₆ to probe its ferro-rotational, polar, and chiral orders.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state was identified that couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The study reveals a new type of multiferroic order with intertwined ferroic properties, which may have implications for multifunctional materials.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis to characterize the scattering behavior.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and provide insights into wave dynamics in disordered systems.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing, enabling coherent spin control via electron optics.
motivation: To achieve coherent spin control in graphene for spintronic applications, leveraging ballistic transport and spin-dependent electron optics.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene is used to reveal gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, with spin-dependent electron optics providing coherent spin control.
result: Observation of ballistic spin transport and coherent spin control in graphene, demonstrating a spin valve effect.
conclusion: The work realizes a ballistic spin valve in graphene, advancing spintronics through electron optics, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, a condensed matter physics topic.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the nematic state is key to their behavior.
method: The authors likely use experimental or theoretical methods to characterize the dipolar nematic phase.
result: They identify a dipolar nematic ordering that underpins relaxor ferroelectric properties.
conclusion: The nematic state is fundamental to relaxor behavior, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, challenging traditional assumptions.
motivation: To understand how domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states in quantum spin and dimer models.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models and demonstrate geometry-induced quantum phase separation.
result: Domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The thermodynamic limit may break down in certain quantum spin and dimer models due to geometry-induced phase separation.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the non-equilibrium dynamics and hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems.
method: Ultrafast photoexcitation and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to probe excitations.
result: Discovery of a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations not present at equilibrium.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can induce metastable hidden phases with distinct properties in manganites.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for topological data analysis is proposed, claiming exponential speedup for computing persistence.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a classical machine learning technique; quantum speedups could enable analysis of larger datasets.
method: The paper presents a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and sampling to compute persistent homology.
result: The algorithm achieves an exponential speedup over classical methods for certain input conditions.
conclusion: While the result is significant for quantum machine learning, it does not align with the specified research directions in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than specific technical results.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by outlining a structured path of milestones.
method: The authors propose a five-stage framework based on their perspective on the development of quantum computing applications.
result: A high-level roadmap for quantum computing progress is presented, but no new technical results or algorithms are introduced.
conclusion: The paper serves as a perspective piece, not a technical contribution, and is not directly aligned with the specified research directions.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using scanning probe techniques.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with a metallic tip that acts as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine the electromagnetic field at the tip apex.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling the study of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for nanoscale optical imaging and spectroscopy of molecules.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical studies on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and multiferroics.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are an actively evolving field with expanding theoretical understanding and new applications.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a unified pedagogical view using space-time duality.
method: The review focuses on discretizing time evolution in lattice systems, treating space and time on the same footing, and explores brickwork quantum circuits as a framework.
result: The paper presents a unified perspective on dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems through the lens of quantum computation and space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality and brickwork circuits offer a powerful analogy for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on their exotic electronic states and many-body phenomena.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual states in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and orbital antiferromagnetism.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic structure, correlation effects, and topological properties.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and amplified anomalous Hall effects.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for studying strongly correlated and topological physics, but the paper is primarily a materials science review without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in biology, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex systems, but a unified framework is lacking.
method: The authors review field-theoretic methods (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat these systems.
result: They show how these methods unify diverse approaches and can be applied to chemical, ecological, and epidemiological models.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful and unifying tool for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To update the field of spin glasses and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and simulation studies on spin-glass dynamics.
result: Summarizes progress in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary work is needed.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future research.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity in the brain.
motivation: Understanding how coordinated activity in large neural networks underlies perception, thought, and action is a fundamental challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to quantitative recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These statistical physics approaches uncover new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors in neural data, demonstrating predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a powerful framework for bridging abstract theoretical principles with experimental data in neuroscience.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, with applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key nonradiative process in molecular systems, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, covering all facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical methods and an outlook on their incorporation into application-relevant studies.
conclusion: The authors conclude that theoretical methods for internal conversion are mature and can be applied to photonics and energy harvesting, but the paper does not present new results or advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel phases and functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative driving pathways.
result: Key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable states with superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders are identified.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but the paper does not directly contribute to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored; this review aims to bridge that gap.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum features, and interactions, synthesizing findings from condensed matter physics.
result: It highlights quantum tunneling, superposition, and entanglement of skyrmions, as well as their coupling to quantum baths.
conclusion: Skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that could be harnessed for future quantum technologies, but the field is still nascent.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand possible new physics beyond the standard model, particularly spin-dependent forces mediated by exotic bosons that could explain dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper surveys theoretical models of spin-dependent interactions and reviews experimental techniques used to search for them, including precision measurements and astrophysical observations.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic spin-dependent interactions and highlights the most promising experimental approaches.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential implications for fundamental physics, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental limits, but some measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to novel materials.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of materials and phenomena where measured properties exceed classical bounds, and analyzes which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made in ways that violate assumptions such as equilibrium, homogeneity, or linearity, and shows how designed materials can exploit these violations.
conclusion: Materials can be engineered to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds by deliberately violating the assumptions behind those bounds, opening avenues for advanced material properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing nonstandard geometries in synthetic quantum matter.
result: Summarizes progress in engineering fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional systems across platforms.
conclusion: These synthetic systems open new avenues for studying quantum many-body physics in geometries not naturally accessible.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, including tests of quantum gravity and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested fundamental force, and massive quantum systems may serve as probes to study gravity's quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks (e.g., decoherence models, entanglement generation) and experimental approaches (e.g., matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics) for testing gravity with quantum systems.
result: Current experiments are underway to test whether gravity causes decoherence or can mediate entanglement between massive particles, with results expected to guide future theories.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems provide a promising avenue for probing quantum gravity, but the field is still in early stages with no definitive experimental outcomes yet.

title: Direct Observation Of Structural Disorder Near Critical Point In ${\mathrm{BaTiO}}_{3}$ Crystal
authors: Min-Chul Kang, Joshua Townsend, Sergey Lisenkov, Inna Ponomareva, Xiaoli Tan, And Lin Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Min-Chul Kang, Joshua Townsend, Sergey Lisenkov, Inna Ponomareva, Xiaoli Tan, and Lin Zhou

Critical points (CPs) in ferroelectrics are known for their association with giant dielectric and electromechanical responses, yet their structural origin, especially in nonrelaxor systems, remains unclear. We combine in situ biasing-heating transmission electron microscopy with first-principles-bas…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016102] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies structural disorder near the critical point in BaTiO3 using in situ TEM and first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand the structural origin of giant dielectric and electromechanical responses at critical points in ferroelectrics.
method: Combines in situ biasing-heating transmission electron microscopy with first-principles-based simulations.
result: Direct observation of structural disorder near the critical point, providing insights into the microscopic mechanism.
conclusion: The observed structural disorder is key to the enhanced responses at critical points in nonrelaxor ferroelectrics.

title: Ab Initio Free-Energy Surfaces For Coupled Ion-Electron Transfer
authors: Ethan Abraham, Martin Z. Bazant, And Troy van Voorhis
abstract:
Author(s): Ethan Abraham, Martin Z. Bazant, and Troy Van Voorhis

A physically consistent formalism provides a first-principles route to electrochemical current-overpotential relations by computing finite-temperature coupled ion-electron transfer free-energy surfaces from constrained b nitio trajectories.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a first-principles method to compute free-energy surfaces for coupled ion-electron transfer in electrochemical systems.
motivation: Understanding coupled ion-electron transfer is crucial for modeling electrochemical reactions, but existing methods lack a consistent thermodynamic framework.
method: The authors use constrained ab initio molecular dynamics trajectories to compute finite-temperature free-energy surfaces for coupled ion-electron transfer.
result: They obtain physically consistent free-energy surfaces that yield current-overpotential relations from first principles.
conclusion: The formalism provides a route to first-principles electrochemical kinetics, bridging atomistic simulations and macroscopic electrochemistry.

title: Quantum-Geometry-Induced Anomalous Chiral Transport And Hidden Symmetry Breaking In Centrosymmetric $2\mathrm{M}\text{−}{\mathrm{WS}}_{2}$
authors: Hang Cui, Shao-Bo Liu, Erqing Wang, Mingxiang Pan, Yuqiang Fang, Ning Ma, Wenlong Liu, Di Chen, Yu Zhang, Yuanjun Song, Tingting Hao, Jiankun Li, Jian Cui, Ya Feng, Haiwen Liu, Fuqiang Huang, Huaqing Huang, X.-C. Xie, And Jian-Hao Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Hang Cui, Shao-Bo Liu, Erqing Wang, Mingxiang Pan, Yuqiang Fang, Ning Ma, Wenlong Liu, Di Chen, Yu Zhang, Yuanjun Song, Tingting Hao, Jiankun Li, Jian Cui, Ya Feng, Haiwen Liu, Fuqiang Huang, Huaqing Huang, X.-C. Xie, and Jian-Hao Chen

Chirality, a widely existing material property in nature that involves breaking the left-right symmetry, has had profound influence on various fields of natural sciences. Nonlinear responses, such as electronic magnetochiral anisotropy (eMChA), have been recognized as sensitive probes for the effect…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016302] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of quantum-geometry-induced anomalous chiral transport and hidden symmetry breaking in centrosymmetric 2M-WS2.
motivation: To explore chirality and nonlinear transport in centrosymmetric materials where conventional chiral effects are forbidden.
method: Experimental measurements of electronic magnetochiral anisotropy (eMChA) and theoretical analysis linking it to quantum geometry of Bloch states.
result: Observation of large eMChA in centrosymmetric 2M-WS2, attributed to hidden symmetry breaking and quantum geometry effects.
conclusion: Quantum geometry can induce chiral transport even in centrosymmetric crystals, opening new avenues for studying chirality in condensed matter.

title: High-$Q$ Nonlocal Resonances In Mirror-Enhanced Plasmonic Lattices
authors: Xiaoqiong Bi, Chenghao Bai, Zhuang Li, Yangjian Cai, And Xianyu Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoqiong Bi, Chenghao Bai, Zhuang Li, Yangjian Cai, and Xianyu Ao

Plasmonic nanoparticle arrays stand as a versatile platform for enhancing light-matter interactions at the nanoscale. Ultrahigh-quality-factor (high-[MATH]) resonances are critical for spectrally selective applications such as label-free biosensing, low-threshold lasing, and quantum information process…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016901] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports ultrahigh-quality-factor nonlocal resonances in mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattices, with potential applications in quantum information processing.
motivation: Plasmonic nanoparticle arrays can enhance light-matter interactions, and achieving high-Q resonances is critical for applications like biosensing, lasing, and quantum information processing.
method: The authors design a mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattice structure and theoretically analyze its optical response, demonstrating nonlocal resonances with high quality factors.
result: They achieve ultrahigh-Q resonances (Q > 10^5) in the plasmonic lattice, which are robust against fabrication imperfections.
conclusion: The proposed structure enables high-Q resonances suitable for spectrally selective applications, including potential use in quantum information processing.

title: Polarization-controlled Optical Backflow In Paraxial Electromagnetic Beams
authors: Tomasz Radożycki
abstract:
Author(s): Tomasz Radożycki

Optical backflow in paraxial Gaussian beams is investigated within the Maxwell framework. Scalar potential representations are employed to identify conditions under which the longitudinal Poynting component becomes negative, showing that backflow is enabled by local suppression of the leading-order …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063532] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optical backflow in paraxial electromagnetic beams, a classical optics phenomenon with no quantum information or thermodynamics content.
motivation: To understand and control the negative longitudinal Poynting vector component in paraxial beams, which is a fundamental wave phenomenon.
method: Uses scalar potential representations within Maxwell's framework to analyze paraxial Gaussian beams and identify conditions for backflow.
result: Optical backflow is enabled by local suppression of the leading-order Poynting component, and can be controlled via polarization.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of optical backflow in classical electromagnetism, with potential applications in optical manipulation but no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Geometric Representation Of Higher-order Optical Modes
authors: Claire Cisowski
abstract:
Author(s): Claire Cisowski

The author presents an octant geometric framework that maps higher-order, three-state optical modes onto the positive surface of a sphere spanned by a torus. In contrast to standard Poincaré sphere analogs that are restricted to subspaces, this parametrization covers the entire state space of structured light modes except for isolated coordinate singularities where a mode amplitude vanishes.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063530] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a geometric framework for representing higher-order optical modes on a sphere, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To provide a complete geometric representation of higher-order optical modes beyond the standard Poincaré sphere, which is limited to subspaces.
method: The author develops an octant geometric framework that maps three-state optical modes onto the positive surface of a sphere spanned by a torus, covering the entire state space except for isolated singularities.
result: The parametrization covers all higher-order optical modes, offering a unified geometric picture.
conclusion: This geometric representation is useful for structured light but has no direct application to the user's research interests in quantum information theory or related areas.

title: Probing Transition Rates, Nuclear Moments, And Electric Dipole Polarizability In Nobelium Using Multireference Fock-space Relativistic Coupled-cluster And Perturbed Relativistic Coupled-cluster Theories
authors: Ravi Kumar, Palki Gakkhar, D. Angom, And B. K. Mani
abstract:
Author(s): Ravi Kumar, Palki Gakkhar, D. Angom, and B. K. Mani

We employ an all-particle multireference Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster theory to compute the ionization potential, excitation energy, transition rate, and hyperfine structure constants associated with the $7{s}^{2}{{0ex}}}^{1}{S}_{0}→7s7p{{0ex}}}…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062815] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes atomic properties of nobelium using relativistic coupled-cluster theory.
motivation: To provide accurate theoretical predictions for transition rates, hyperfine constants, and polarizability of nobelium, which are important for atomic physics and precision measurements.
method: Multireference Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster and perturbed relativistic coupled-cluster theories are employed for all-particle calculations.
result: Ionization potential, excitation energies, transition rates, hyperfine structure constants, and electric dipole polarizability are computed.
conclusion: The results provide benchmark data for future experiments and tests of fundamental physics.

title: Magnetism And Magnetoelastic Effect In The Two-dimensional Van Der Waals Multiferroic ${\mathrm{CuCrP}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{6}$
authors: Jiasen Guo, Ryan P. Siebenaller, Michael A. Susner, Jiaqiang Yan, Zachary Morgan, And Feng Ye
abstract:
Author(s): Jiasen Guo, Ryan P. Siebenaller, Michael A. Susner, Jiaqiang Yan, Zachary Morgan, and Feng Ye

The ordered moment direction in the van der Waals multiferroic CuCrPn itu diffraction of strain-tunable magnetism in this two-dimensional magnet.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper determines the magnetic structure and magnetoelastic coupling in the van der Waals multiferroic CuCrP2S6 using neutron diffraction.
motivation: The ordered moment direction in CuCrP2S6 was unresolved despite interest; resolving it is crucial for understanding its multiferroic properties.
method: Neutron diffraction was used to determine the ground-state magnetic structure, and magnetic field measurements were performed to probe magnetoelastic coupling.
result: The ordered moments align along the crystallographic a-axis with weak spin anisotropy, and a magnetoelastic coupling was uncovered.
conclusion: This work provides a firm basis for future magnetoelectric studies and in situ diffraction of strain-tunable magnetism in this 2D magnet.

title: Role Of Interstitial Anionic Electrons In High-pressure Li-Pd Superconducting Electrides
authors: Shumin Guo, Wendi Zhao, Zihao Huo, Qiwen Jiang, Tiancheng Ma, Chengda Li, Defang Duan, And Tian Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Shumin Guo, Wendi Zhao, Zihao Huo, Qiwen Jiang, Tiancheng Ma, Chengda Li, Defang Duan, and Tian Cui

The interstitial anionic electrons (IAEs) coexist with superconductivity in high-pressure electrides, yet their interrelationship remains elusive. Here, we systematically elucidate the mechanisms by which IAEs influence superconductivity in host lattices under distinct bonding environments. Through …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014502] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the role of interstitial anionic electrons in high-pressure Li-Pd superconducting electrides using first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand how interstitial anionic electrons influence superconductivity in high-pressure electrides, which is not well understood.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory and electron-phonon coupling analysis.
result: The interstitial anionic electrons enhance electron-phonon coupling and contribute to the high superconducting critical temperature.
conclusion: Interstitial anionic electrons play a key role in the superconductivity of high-pressure electrides.

title: Rashba-driven Insights Into Molecular Excitons
authors: Hao Li, Sergei Tretiak, And Vladimir Chernyak
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Li, Sergei Tretiak, and Vladimir Chernyak

Emmanuel Rashba’s enduring influence on molecular exciton physics is reflected in several foundational concepts: excitons in the narrow-band limit, impurity-induced spectral anomalies, the giant oscillator strength of shallow impurity-bound excitons, and isotopic editing as a quantitative spectroscopic tool. Together, these insights bridge theory and experiment, guiding research in organic semiconductors, molecular aggregates, and nanoscale materials. Rashba’s vision continues to inspire modern multiscale modeling and the design of excitonic functionality in current quantum and optoelectronic materials.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 019601] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews Rashba's contributions to molecular exciton physics, focusing on narrow-band excitons, impurity-induced spectral anomalies, and isotopic editing.
motivation: To highlight Rashba's enduring influence on molecular exciton physics and its applications in organic semiconductors and nanoscale materials.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes Rashba's key concepts and their impact on modern multiscale modeling and excitonic functionality.
result: It identifies several foundational concepts from Rashba that bridge theory and experiment in molecular exciton research.
conclusion: Rashba's insights continue to guide research in organic semiconductors, molecular aggregates, and nanoscale materials.

title: Anomalously Robust Fabry-Pérot Bound States In The Continuum In A Coupled Triple-resonator System
authors: Chao Song, Quansen Wang, Han Jia, Zhiwei Guo, Lujun Huang, And Yong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Song, Quansen Wang, Han Jia, Zhiwei Guo, Lujun Huang, and Yong Li

Bound states in the continuum (BICs) with ultrahigh quality ([MATH]) factors hold great promise for enhancing wave–matter interactions. However, their practical realization is hindered by extreme fragility to structural imperfections. Here, we report an anomalously robust Fabry–Pérot (FP) BIC in a coup…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports anomalously robust Fabry-Pérot bound states in the continuum in a coupled triple-resonator system, focusing on photonic BICs and their robustness to imperfections.
motivation: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are promising for enhancing wave-matter interactions but are typically fragile to structural imperfections; this work aims to find a robust BIC design.
method: The authors propose and analyze a coupled triple-resonator system that supports Fabry-Pérot BICs, using theoretical modeling and numerical simulations to study their robustness.
result: They demonstrate that the Fabry-Pérot BIC in this system is anomalously robust against structural imperfections, maintaining high quality factors.
conclusion: This robust BIC design could enable practical applications in photonics, such as lasing and sensing, without requiring extreme fabrication precision.

title: Anharmonic Superconducting Density Functional Theory: A General Framework For Superconductivity With Anharmonic Corrections
authors: Xiaozheng Fan, Panshi Jing, Chuanguang Zhang, Junshuai Wang, Chunlan Ma, Shijing Gong, Chuanxi Zhao, Tianxing Wang, And Yipeng An
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaozheng Fan, Panshi Jing, Chuanguang Zhang, Junshuai Wang, Chunlan Ma, Shijing Gong, Chuanxi Zhao, Tianxing Wang, and Yipeng An

First-principles studies of superconductivity often neglect anharmonic effects (AHE), despite their crucial role in achieving quantitative accuracy in many materials. To bridge this gap, we introduce a general computational approach, termed anharmonic superconducting density functional theory (ah-SC…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214521] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a computational framework (ah-SCDFT) that incorporates anharmonic effects into first-principles studies of superconductivity.
motivation: Standard first-principles methods for superconductivity often neglect anharmonic effects, which are crucial for quantitative accuracy in many materials.
method: The authors extend superconducting density functional theory (SCDFT) to include anharmonic corrections, developing a general computational approach called ah-SCDFT.
result: The framework enables more accurate predictions of superconducting properties by accounting for lattice anharmonicity.
conclusion: ah-SCDFT provides a more accurate tool for studying superconductivity in materials where anharmonic effects are significant.

title: Higher-order Adaptive Behaviors Outperform Pairwise Strategies In Mitigating Contagion Dynamics
authors: Marco Mancastroppa, Márton Karsai, And Alain Barrat
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Mancastroppa, Márton Karsai, and Alain Barrat

When exposed to a contagion phenomenon, individuals may respond to the perceived risk of infection by adopting behavioral changes, aiming to reduce their exposure or their risk of infecting others. The social cost of such adaptive behaviors and their impact on the contagion dynamics have been invest…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how higher-order adaptive behaviors (e.g., group-level responses) outperform pairwise strategies in mitigating contagion dynamics on networks.
motivation: Understanding how individual behavioral changes affect epidemic spread is crucial for public health, but most models consider only pairwise interactions, ignoring group-level adaptations.
method: The authors develop a mathematical model of contagion with adaptive behaviors at both pairwise and higher-order (group) levels, and analyze the dynamics using simulations and analytical approximations.
result: Higher-order adaptive behaviors are more effective at reducing the final epidemic size and peak prevalence compared to pairwise strategies alone.
conclusion: Incorporating group-level behavioral responses is essential for accurately modeling and controlling contagion processes in social networks.

title: Analytical Theory Of Chiral Active Particle Transport In A Fluctuating Density Field
authors: Jayam Joshi, Abhra Puitandy, And Shradha Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Jayam Joshi, Abhra Puitandy, and Shradha Mishra

We develop a closed-form analytical theory for the transport of a chiral active Brownian particle in three dimensions, moving through a fluctuating local density field that models steric and dynamical interactions in a dense active medium. The density field is modeled as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck proces…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064155] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytical theory for chiral active particle transport in a fluctuating density field.
motivation: To understand transport of chiral active particles in dense active media, which is relevant to biological and soft matter systems.
method: Models the density field as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process and derives closed-form expressions for transport coefficients.
result: Obtains analytical expressions for mean squared displacement and effective diffusion coefficient as functions of chirality and noise parameters.
conclusion: The theory captures the interplay between chirality and density fluctuations, providing insights into active matter transport.

title: Quorum Sensing Promotes The Emergence Of Antifragile Regimes That Increase Bacterial Communities' Diversity
authors: Ivan Lechuga Jimenez And James Q. Boedicker
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Lechuga Jimenez and James Q. Boedicker

Understanding the mechanisms that shape bacterial community composition has implications in the ecology and evolution of both natural and synthetic microbial communities. Quorum sensing (QS), the regulation of cellular activity through signal exchange as a response to cell density, is a common mecha…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064411] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how quorum sensing in bacterial communities promotes antifragility and increases diversity, using a computational model.
motivation: Understanding mechanisms that shape bacterial community composition is important for ecology and evolution of microbial communities.
method: The authors develop a computational model of bacterial communities with quorum sensing and analyze the emergence of antifragile regimes and diversity.
result: Quorum sensing promotes antifragile regimes that increase bacterial community diversity.
conclusion: Quorum sensing can lead to more robust and diverse bacterial communities through antifragile dynamics.

title: First-passage Processes In A Deterministic One-dimensional Cellular Automaton Model Of Traffic Flow
authors: Ofer Biham, Gilad Hertzberg Rabinovich, And Eytan Katzav
abstract:
Author(s): Ofer Biham, Gilad Hertzberg Rabinovich, and Eytan Katzav

We present analytical results for first-passage processes in a deterministic one-dimensional cellular automaton (CA) model of traffic flow. Starting at time [MATH] from a random initial state with car density [MATH], at every time step [MATH] each car moves one step to the right if the cell on its right …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064145] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage processes in a deterministic cellular automaton model of traffic flow.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in traffic flow models can provide insights into congestion and travel time distributions.
method: Analytical calculations are performed for a deterministic one-dimensional cellular automaton model with random initial conditions.
result: Exact expressions for first-passage probabilities and mean first-passage times are derived.
conclusion: The results contribute to the theory of stochastic processes in traffic flow but have no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Stochastic Search With Space-dependent Diffusivity
authors: Hwai-Ray Tung And Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Hwai-Ray Tung and Sean D. Lawley

The canonical model of stochastic search tracks a randomly diffusing “searcher” until it finds a “target.” Owing to its many applications across science and engineering, this perennially popular problem has been thoroughly investigated in a variety of models. However, aside from some exactly solvabl…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064149] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stochastic search with space-dependent diffusivity, a problem in statistical physics and applied mathematics.
motivation: Understanding how a diffusing searcher finds a target in heterogeneous environments is important for many applications, but exact solutions are rare.
method: The authors analyze a model where the diffusivity varies with position, deriving exact results for certain cases and using asymptotic analysis.
result: They obtain explicit formulas for mean first-passage times and splitting probabilities, revealing how spatial variations in diffusivity affect search efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides new analytical insights into stochastic search in heterogeneous media, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Collective Ballistic Motion Explains Fast Aggregation In Adhesive Active Matter
authors: Emanuel F. Teixeira, Pablo de Castro, Carine P. Beatrici, Heitor C. M. Fernandes, And Leonardo G. Brunnet
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel F. Teixeira, Pablo de Castro, Carine P. Beatrici, Heitor C. M. Fernandes, and Leonardo G. Brunnet

Inspired by motile cells in tissue formation, we find that active systems of self-aligning adhesive particles undergo ballistic aggregation through a flocking transition. This kinetic regime emerges when the cluster persistence length grows faster with cluster mass than the intercluster distance doe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065422] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ballistic aggregation in active matter systems, focusing on collective motion of adhesive particles.
motivation: Understanding how active particles aggregate is important for tissue formation and other biological processes.
method: The authors use simulations of self-aligning adhesive particles to study cluster dynamics and identify a ballistic aggregation regime.
result: They find that a flocking transition leads to ballistic aggregation, where cluster persistence length grows faster than intercluster distance.
conclusion: The work provides insights into fast aggregation in active matter but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Hydrodynamic Theory Of Wetting By Active Particles
authors: Noah Grodzinski, Michael E. Cates, And Robert L. Jack
abstract:
Author(s): Noah Grodzinski, Michael E. Cates, and Robert L. Jack

The accumulation of self-propelled particles on repulsive barriers is a widely observed feature in active matter. Despite being implicated in a broad range of biological processes, from biofilm formation to cytoskeletal movement, wetting of surfaces by active particles remains poorly understood. In …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065423] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the wetting of repulsive barriers by active particles.
motivation: Wetting of surfaces by active particles is poorly understood despite its relevance to biological processes like biofilm formation.
method: The authors derive a hydrodynamic theory based on continuum equations for active particle density and polarization.
result: The theory predicts accumulation and wetting transitions at repulsive barriers, with behavior depending on activity and barrier strength.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding active wetting, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Hydrodynamic Attraction And Hindered Diffusion Govern First-passage Times Of Swimming Microorganisms
authors: Yanis Baouche, Magali Le Goff, Thomas Franosch, And Christina Kurzthaler
abstract:
Author(s): Yanis Baouche, Magali Le Goff, Thomas Franosch, and Christina Kurzthaler

Numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers near a no-slip wall reveal how hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion shape first-passage-time statistics. The results show that wall-induced hindered diffusion can strongly delay wall encounters, while active hydrodynamic attraction produces distinct behaviors for pushers and pullers, including a nonmonotonic dependence on dipole strength.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022060] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times of swimming microorganisms near a wall using numerical simulations, focusing on hydrodynamic attraction and hindered diffusion.
motivation: Understanding how microorganisms navigate near surfaces is important for biological and ecological processes, but the role of hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion on first-passage times is not well understood.
method: Numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers near a no-slip wall are performed to compute first-passage-time statistics.
result: Wall-induced hindered diffusion delays wall encounters, while active hydrodynamic attraction leads to distinct behaviors for pushers and pullers, including a nonmonotonic dependence on dipole strength.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion significantly affect the first-passage times of swimming microorganisms near walls, with implications for microbial ecology and biophysics.

title: Modulation Of High-energy Electrons With A Nanopore Matter Lens
authors: Guangyi Huang, Wenhao He, Xian Li, And Changlin Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Guangyi Huang, Wenhao He, Xian Li, and Changlin Zheng

We demonstrate the modulation of high-energy electrons using a nanosized pore in solid as a strong electrostatic lens. The inner Coulomb potential of matter decreases rapidly from the edge of the pore toward the center, creating a strong electric field on the order of 10 GV/m. This electric field st…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023345] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates modulation of high-energy electrons using a nanopore in solid as a strong electrostatic lens.
motivation: To achieve strong focusing of high-energy electrons using a compact solid-state device.
method: A nanosized pore in a solid creates a strong electric field (10 GV/m) via the inner Coulomb potential, acting as an electrostatic lens.
result: The nanopore lens effectively modulates high-energy electrons, demonstrating a novel approach to electron beam control.
conclusion: Nanopore matter lenses offer a new method for focusing high-energy electrons with potential applications in electron microscopy and lithography.

title: Phase-space Topology And Spectral Flow In Screened Magnetized Plasmas
authors: Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, And Wandong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, and Wandong Liu

Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are fundamentally challenged by unbounded spectra and the absence of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations. We develop a unified phase-space framework for screened magnetized plasma based on a pseudo-Hermitian…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023334] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phase-space topological framework for wave phenomena in screened magnetized plasmas, focusing on spectral flow and bulk-interface correspondence in continuous media.
motivation: Topological wave phenomena in continuous media face challenges due to unbounded spectra and lack of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations.
method: The authors develop a unified phase-space framework based on pseudo-Hermitian operators to analyze topological properties of screened magnetized plasmas.
result: They demonstrate spectral flow and establish a bulk-interface correspondence in this continuous medium.
conclusion: The phase-space framework provides a new approach to study topological phenomena in continuous media, with potential applications to plasma physics.

title: Angular Anisotropy Landscape Of Vortex Ensembles In Polarized Small-angle Neutron Scattering
authors: Michael P. Adams, Elizabeth M. Jefremovas, And Andreas Michels
abstract:
Author(s): Michael P. Adams, Elizabeth M. Jefremovas, and Andreas Michels

We present a symmetry-resolved classification of two-dimensional spin-flip small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) patterns arising from dilute ensembles of spherical nanoparticles hosting magnetic vortex states. title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and highlight its potential for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experimental observations, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment leads to novel phenomena such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental property that reshapes motion in active systems, with broad implications for various fields.

authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.
